subject: Career
title: Knowing When to Walk Away
description: A quick, practical guide to Knowing When to Walk Away.

hook.text: They won't budge. You've tried three times. At some point, negotiation ends and decision begins.

buildup.text: Your BATNA — best alternative to a negotiated agreement — determines your walk-away power.

discovery.text: If your alternative is strong (another offer, current job you like), walking away is easy.

twist.text: If you have no alternative, your leverage disappears. Build alternatives before you need them.

climax.text: Walking away with grace keeps the door open. 'I respect the offer but need X to make this work.'

punchline.text: The power to walk away is the power to negotiate.

quiz.question: What determines your walk-away power in negotiation?
options: Your BATNA — best alternative to a negotiated agreement

details.summary: Knowing your walk-away point, the minimum acceptable offer, before entering a negotiation provides clarity and prevents desperation-driven decisions. The strongest negotiators have a clear BATNA, or best alternative to a negotiated agreement, which gives them genuine confidence.
details.whyItMatters: Without a defined walk-away point, you risk accepting offers that undervalue you simply because they are on the table. Clarity on your floor preserves long-term career value.
takeaways: Define your minimum acceptable offer before any negotiation
A strong BATNA increases your confidence and your outcome
Walking away from a bad offer protects long-term earning power

faq.question: How do I determine my walk-away point for a specific negotiation?
faq.answer: Calculate your minimum financial needs including bills, savings targets, and debt payments. Then add your market value floor based on research. The higher of these two numbers is your walk-away point. Never negotiate below your survival number.

faq.question: What if walking away means unemployment for an extended period?
faq.answer: If your financial runway is short, your walk-away point adjusts downward pragmatically. Consider accepting a lower offer with a six-month renegotiation clause. Securing income while planning your next move is sometimes the most strategic choice.
